sentences.text: 3. All these appeals have been filed by the Insurance Company challenging liability to pay the compensation as imposed by the Tribunal and for setting aside principle of pay and recover applied by Tribunal.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant, after referring to Insurance policy (Ex.D/1) and depositions of non-applicant witness Smt. Ichha Dixit, submits that in the instant case, Insurance policy was Act only policy.
Therefore, Insurance Company is liable to pay upto Rs.1,00,000/- and principle of pay and recover cannot be applied.

Further, it is also urged that in death case, Insurance Company is liable to pay Rs.1,00,000/- and in injury case, it is not liable to pay any amount.
5.
I have heard learned counsel for the appellant and perused the record of the case.

6. Perusal of deposition of non-applicant witness Smt. Ichha Dixit and Insurance policy (Ex.D/1)
reveal that "it is private car liability only policy" and not comprehensive/package policy.
It is also evident from above that Insurance Company has received total premium of Rs.450/- for nine passengers, Rs.50/- for each passenger.
7. Hence, in view of above, Insurance policy being only policy, principle of pay and recover cannot be applied.

(National Insurance Co. Ltd Vs. Balakrishnan and another 2013 (1) SCC 731 , General Manager, United India Insurance Co. Ltd Vs. M. Laxmi and others 2009 (17) SCC 301 and M.A.No.5762 of 2019 HDFC Ergo General Insurance Company Vs. Smt. Dumri Bai dated 11.07.2022 relied.

sentences.text: Hence, findings of Tribunal with respect to pay and recover are set aside.

8. So far as Insurance Company's liability in relation to quantum of compensation/extent of evidence under Insurance policy Ex.D/1 is concerned, in this connection, IMT-16 (D/1) is important and it reads as under:-
"IMT 16. Personal accident to unnamed passengers other than Insured and the paid driver and cleaner (For vehicles rated as Private cars and Motorized two wheelers)

In consideration of the payment it is hereby understood and agreed that the insurer undertakes to pay compensation on the scale provided below for bodily injuries hereinafter defines sustained by any passenger other than the insured and/or the paid driver attendant or cleaner and/or a person in the employ of the insured coming within the scope of the Workmens Compensation Act, 1923 and subsequent amendments of the said Act and engaged in and upon the service of the insured at the time such injury is sustained whilst mounting into, dismounting, from or travelling in but not driving the insured motor car and caused by violent, accidental, external and visible means which independently of any other cause shall within three calendar months of the occurrence of such injury result in :
 Death of Injury Scale of compensatio  i) Death 100%
 ii) Loss of two limbs or sight of two  eyes or one limb and sight of one eye 100%
 iii) Loss of one limb or sight of one eye 50%

4 iv) Permanent Total Disablement from injuries other than named above 100%"
9.

sentences.text:
Thus, from above, it is evident that in case of death, Insurance Company is liable to pay 100%
compensation i.e. upto Rs.1,00,000/- but therein, (IMT-16) simple injuries or grievous injuries are not covered.
Hence, Insurance Company is not liable to pay any compensation to claimant Guddu Patel.
He has suffered grievous injuries only but no permanent disablement of any kind whatsoever.
10. Hence, in view of above, appeal filed by appellant is allowed and it is held that principle of pay and recover as applied by the Tribunal is set aside.

Further, it is held that Insurance Company is liable to pay Rs. 1,00,000/- to claimants in MACC No.2097/2019 (Smt. Chaina Bai and Others Vs.
Kamlesh Chaudhary a n d Others) and Rs.1,00,000/- to claimants in MACC No.2098/2019 (Smt.
Meera Bai and Others Vs. Kamlesh Chaudhary and Others) but Insurance Company is not liable to pay any compensation in MACC No.2142 of 2019 (Smt. Guddu Patel Vs. Kamlesh Chaudhary) as Guddu Patel did not suffer any injuries as mentioned in IMT-16 (Ex/D/1)
11.

sentences.text: Claimant Guddu is entitled to receive compensation as determined by Tribunal from owner and driver of offending vehicle jointly and severely.
Similarly as Insurance Company is liable to pay Rs.1,00,000/- to Chaina Bai and other claimants out of Rs.11,45,200/- and Rs.1,00,000/- to Meera Bai and other claimants out of Rs.6,50,800/-.
Remaining amount in Claim Case Nos. 2097/2019 and 2098/2019 shall be paid by owner and driver of offending vehicle jointly and severely.
12. Appeal filed by appellant is allowed and disposed off accordingly.
